# Goban Studio v12.0.0

v12 undoes a step backwards. Since v9 the app had two spaces, and the
start of every day — what to play, what to practise, where your games are
— was harder to find than before. v12 brings back the four places from
before v9, on top of what v9–v11 did well, and withdraws two v11
additions that lowered the quality. v12 reads everything v11 saved.

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of every file. Windows on ARM runs the x64
build under the system's emulation.

## Four places again

- **Today** (⌘1) — the app opens here: the game in progress or the
  suggested game with one button, today's practice (or the placement quiz
  first), your level, this week, and your last three games.
- **Play** (⌘2) — the board. With no game on it, the suggested game and
  New game.
- **Practice** (⌘3) — today's path, and on the same page the whole course
  and every problem by topic (no longer one click away).
- **Library** (⌘4) — your games, the twenty classics and the opening
  explorer; Import SGF.

The game panel shows your level next to "You" again.

Kept from v9–v11: the player model and its estimate, the opponent chosen
as one measured rank, the post-game review with *Try again*, the
placement quiz, the new mark, and the *Practise these* link from a review
takeaway.

## Withdrawn from v11

- **The 81 problems added in v11.** Many were not positions a player
  would meet: a few stones scattered on an open board. The bank is the
  543 problems of v10 again. Your progress on the withdrawn problems is
  no longer shown.
- **The classics' engine rows.** Rows like "About 5 points lost" said
  nothing a learner could use. Each classic keeps only the famous moves
  written for it (the ear-reddening move, Go Seigen's opening, Shusai's
  move 160, Lee Sedol's move 78, Ke Jie's early 3-3 invasion).

## Known limits

- The builds are not code-signed (no certificates yet). The update
  checksum guards against damaged or wrong downloads; it is not a
  signature.
- Not yet checked by people: a usability test of the four places, a
  strong player's review of the course, a native-speaker review of the
  Chinese, Korean and Japanese text, and a real screen-reader session.
- *Try again* needs KataGo (the desktop app); the browser preview has no
  KataGo.
- The KataGo check of the course leaves some steps for a human.
- The counting solver ignores ko threats; endgame problems avoid ko.
- The value of a handicap stone is the conventional one on every board;
  on 13×13 a measurement between programs disagrees (`docs/strength.md`),
  and no people were measured.
